question: A 45-year-old male presents to his primary care physician for complaints of dizziness. The patient reports he experiences room-spinning dizziness lasting several hours at a time, approximately 2-3 times a month, starting 3 months ago. Upon questioning, the patient also reports right sided diminished hearing, tinnitus, and a sensation of ear fullness. Her temperature is 99 deg F (37.2 deg C), pulse 70/min, respirations 12, blood pressure 130 mmHg/85 mmHg, SpO2 99%. You decide to order an audiometric evaluation. What is the most likely finding of the audiogram?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Room-spinning dizziness lasting several hours" -> "Episodic vertigo" -> "Possible Meniere's disease" -> 70% CHAIN: "Right-sided diminished hearing, tinnitus, ear fullness" -> "Symptoms of inner ear pathology" -> "Possible Meniere's disease" -> 80% CHAIN: "Temperature 99 deg F, pulse 70/min, blood pressure 130/85 mmHg" -> "Normal vital signs" -> "Unlikely systemic infection" -> 90% CHAIN: "Ordering an audiometric evaluation" -> "Assessment of hearing function" -> "Investigation for hearing loss etiology" -> 80% CHAIN: "Audiometric evaluation in Meniere's disease" -> "Low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss" -> 70%
analysis: The patient's presentation of room-spinning dizziness, right-sided diminished hearing, tinnitus, and ear fullness is suggestive of Meniere's disease. Meniere's disease typically presents with low-frequency sensorineural hearing loss, along with other symptoms like vertigo and tinnitus.
